meaning: To initiate conversation in a social situation
example: He told a joke to break the ice at the party.

phrase: Hit the nail on the head
meaning: To describe exactly what is causing a problem
example: You hit the nail on the head with that analysis.

meaning: To endure a painful situation with courage
example: Just bite the bullet and go to the dentist.

meaning: To reveal secret information accidentally
example: Don't spill the beans about the surprise party.

meaning: Feeling ill or unwell
example: I'm feeling a bit under the weather today.

meaning: To go to bed
example: I'm exhausted, I'm going to hit the sack.

meaning: Very rarely
example: She visits her hometown once in a blue moon.

meaning: To work late into the night
example: He burned the midnight oil to finish the report.

phrase: Cost an arm and a leg
meaning: To be very expensive
example: That handbag costs an arm and a leg.

phrase: Let the cat out of the bag
meaning: To accidentally reveal a secret
example: She let the cat out of the bag about the promotion.

phrase: The ball is in your court
meaning: It is up to you to make the next decision
example: I've made my offer — the ball is in your court.

phrase: Bite off more than you can chew
meaning: To take on more responsibility than you can handle
example: Don't bite off more than you can chew with five projects.

phrase: Kill two birds with one stone
meaning: To accomplish two things with one action
example: I killed two birds with one stone by exercising during my commute.

meaning: To miss an opportunity
example: You missed the boat on that investment.

meaning: To give up or admit defeat
example: After three failed attempts, he threw in the towel.

meaning: To avoid taking sides in a disagreement
example: You can't sit on the fence on this issue.

meaning: Done secretly, especially involving bribery
example: The deal was made under the table.

meaning: Undecided or uncommitted
example: I'm still on the fence about moving to London.

meaning: To become uncontrollable
example: The situation got out of hand quickly.

phrase: Give the benefit of the doubt
meaning: To trust someone despite uncertainty
example: Let's give him the benefit of the doubt.

phrase: Bite the hand that feeds you
meaning: To harm someone who is helping you
example: Don't bite the hand that feeds you by criticising your sponsor.

meaning: Said when someone appears just after being mentioned
example: Speak of the devil — here comes John!

phrase: Get a taste of your own medicine
meaning: Experience the same treatment you give others
example: He finally got a taste of his own medicine.

meaning: To stop yourself from saying something
example: I had to bite my tongue during the meeting.
